neighbours.label: the full stop that closes a sentence reporting growth between two dated figures ('from 3,000 in 1950 to more than 40,000 in 2010.'), as against full stops after other sentences, including other number sentences
fire: Officials said the city expanded from 8,000 people in 1920 to nearly 90,000 in 2000. Schools struggled to keep up.
According to the report, enrollment went from 1,200 students in 1985 to over 6,000 in 2015. New buildings followed.
The census shows the county grew from 15,000 residents in 1940 to about 120,000 in 2020. Traffic is now a problem.
In short, the herd recovered from 300 animals in 1970 to more than 5,000 in 2012. Hunting was banned in that period.
The data show that exports climbed from $2 million in 1990 to $45 million in 2018. Most went to Europe.
Since its founding, the club grew from 40 members in 1965 to almost 3,000 in 2005. It now has its own stadium.
Records show the village shrank from 2,500 people in 1900 to fewer than 300 in 1990. Many houses stand empty.
Over time, the library's collection rose from 10,000 books in 1955 to over 400,000 in 2010. It needed a new wing.
quiet: Officials said the city is planning a new park near the river. Schools welcomed the news.
According to the report, enrollment is stable and classes are full. New buildings are not needed.
The census shows the county is mostly rural with small farms. Traffic is light.
In short, the herd is healthy and grazes on the northern slopes. Hunting is banned there.
The data show that exporters prefer shipping by sea. Most goods go to Europe.
Since its founding, the club has played in green shirts. It now has its own stadium.
Records show the village had a mill and a small church. Many houses are old.
Over time, the library added a reading room and a cafe. It needed a new wing.
